subject: Immunization
title: Vaccine Types, Cold Chain & Contraindications
preview: Vaccine effectiveness depends on product-specific storage, correct handling and age-appropriate administration.

sections.title: Recognize vaccine platforms
points: Live attenuated vaccines contain weakened organisms; inactivated and recombinant platforms do not contain replication-competent live pathogens.
Conjugation enhances immune responses to selected polysaccharide antigens, especially in young children.

sections.title: Practical storage principles
points: Many refrigerator-stored vaccines require a controlled 2–8°C range, but product labeling and national guidance determine exact conditions.
Freeze-sensitive products should not be stored where accidental freezing can occur; temperature monitoring and documented handling are essential.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: “Refrigerated” does not mean every vaccine has identical storage requirements.
Do not assume an accidental temperature excursion is harmless or automatically discard stock before contacting responsible authorities.

quickRevision: Vaccines include live attenuated, inactivated, toxoid, recombinant and conjugate formulations.
Cold-chain requirements are specific to the product; freezing can permanently damage certain vaccines.
If a temperature excursion occurs, quarantine affected doses and follow program/manufacturer advice before use or disposal.

quiz.question: What is a principle of vaccine cold-chain management?
options: Use any storage refrigerator without monitoring
quiz.explanation: Continuous product-appropriate temperature control. Many refrigerator-stored vaccines require a controlled 2–8°C range, but product labeling and national guidance determine exact conditions.
